pipeline: sealed Build animation policy (layers or graph) -> fixed spatial Tick -> existing VSR layer/graph evaluator -> animationRoot/frameRoot -> web-release target -> Chromium WebGPU

semanticOwners.realityStudio: Reality Studio Sequencer v1.7 remains the authored presentation timeline owner; the raw Build fixture has no sequencer field and no Sequence playback lowering was inferred.
semanticOwners.vsr: Visual State Runtime owns animation layers, blend/mask semantics, animation graph state/transition sampling and frame compilation.
semanticOwners.rsr: Reality Simulation Runtime remains the authoritative spatial state and Tick owner; it does not receive presentation animation policy writes.
semanticOwners.realityBuild: Reality Build owns candidate validation, fixed-Tick lowering and target/evidence projection; it does not evaluate animation semantics itself.

existingContracts: VSR sampleSpatialAnimationLayers() already covers override, additive and node mask behavior.
VSR sampleSpatialAnimationGraph() already covers declared states and deterministic transitions.
VSR compileSpatialFrame() gives graph precedence over layers and layers precedence over a single clip, and roots the selected animation inputs.
Studio Sequence evaluation produces presentation roots, but Build has no sequence consumer and the source fixture materializes a default sequence only inside a Studio session.
archaeology.gap: The Build seam previously carried only a flat fixed-tick clip policy; layers and graph selections were present in VSR but could not cross the candidate target boundary.

candidate.lowering: layers -> VSR animationLayers with one fixed time per layer; graph -> VSR animationGraph with declared state ids and optional static transition; clip policy remains backward compatible.
candidate.authorityBoundary: Candidate-only presentation policy; RSR state/clock remains authoritative; VSR remains the animation evaluator and frame-root owner.

tests.candidateNegativeCases: PASS; unsupported wall-clock mode, missing clip, invalid layer weight and invalid graph initial state fail closed

missingCapability: A shared RCL-level animation presentation contract and authored Sequence-to-target lowering are not yet established; this candidate only lowers existing VSR layer/graph selections through a fixed Tick.
currentWorkaround: Reality Build validates a candidate-only policy, maps its time to the authoritative spatial Tick, and delegates layers/graph evaluation to VSR. Projects without a policy retain the legacy path.
donorAdvantage: VSR already provides deterministic layer blending, additive offsets, masks, graph transitions, animation roots and frame verification; Studio already provides authored Sequence roots but has no Build consumer in this path.
candidateAbsorption: Do not silently move Build policy into RCL Core or create a second sequence evaluator. Preserve Studio/VSR/RSR ownership and revisit a shared RCL presentation primitive only after cross-target replay and authority review.
regressionCase: Legacy flat clip policy remains compatible; malformed selection/layer/graph policies fail closed; sourceRealityRoot remains stable while animationRoot/frameRoot change across fixed ticks.
boundaries: All graph/layer policies and frame outputs are candidate-only and non-authoritative.
Chromium WebGPU proves local browser execution, not physical-device GPU parity, frame-rate SLA, native target parity or release delivery.
Studio authored Sequence tracks are inspected but not lowered or played by Build; a static graph transition is not a full behavior-driven animation state machine.
No audio cue-to-asset mapping, decode, mixing, Android APK/runtime, physical device, WAN transport, production asset service or human acceptance is claimed.
No K400 gate is promoted to PASS; the listed cells identify affected evidence surfaces only.
nextCandidate: Audit the shared authored presentation spine: determine whether Studio Sequence clips can be explicitly projected into the existing VSR/Build seam without duplicating timeline ownership; keep audio separately blocked until cue-to-asset canonical ownership and receipt shape are decided.
